gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: The page only requires that q not divide the denominator xi. The conclusion is stronger than that and does not follow: a zero entry has numerator 0, which q divides. What is actually needed is that q divide no denominator of F_1, F_2 or their inverses (which also forces the diagonal numerators to be prime to q). The page never says the inverses' denominators are covered.

False for the listed operations. Starting from (eta,zeta): D+=H gives (eta,zeta+eta); the swap gives (zeta+eta,eta); D-=H gives (zeta+eta,-zeta). So the pair becomes (eta+zeta,-zeta), and D_tau is negated rather than unchanged. A correct third step is D_tau <- H_sigma - D_tau (or an extra negation).

gaps.quote: So the shear needs $2\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
gaps.note: Inconsistent with the page. Each update takes one interchange and there are rank_Q M ones in Pi, so the count is rank_Q M, not twice that. The later definition of s_b as the sum of the ranks also counts one per rank.

gaps.term: linear cost of a lower-triangular pass
gaps.quote: The coefficients come from the finitely many matrices, not from $V$, and $R$ is fixed, so each pass is linear.
gaps.note: The cited O(V) cost is stated, but the page never says why multiplying a field by a rational mu/xi, which acts as mu times xi^{-1} mod q^b, is linear in the field's length. The residue xi^{-1} mod q^b has b digits and depends on b, so it is not a fixed constant. Linearity needs this to be a multiplication by the small integer mu and an exact division by the small integer xi, which the page does not state.

The formula is neither derived nor marked as cited. The rank budget, wires, negative source projections and decreasing edges are never defined, so the reader cannot check the identity or see what N and L_b count.
